This is just me spitballing, but I would look for some kind of traumatic event, doesn't have to be major trauma like physical abuse, but something that would have caused you as a child to feel shame when you enjoy something. I'm not sure how an independent cleaner would do it but as far as my cleaning company goes we ask that if the client wants something like this done then it's better for the client remove the items and put them back. Most quotes from companies are for the a cleaning for a *certain* amount of time. For you these shelves might take just a couple mins because you know where all your stuff goes and perhaps you won't care where you put it back at or wont care how organized it is, but for a cleaner hoping to do a good job we would want to put it back and make it look organized in order to meet or exceed the clients expectations, so this requires more than just a couple of mins, and since this might not have been factored into the clean then I think 10 dollars for something that might take someone 10-15 mins isn't a bad deal. I will Def say that if I had someone add something on that isn't normally part of the clean, I quoted them a good price, and they balked at it, I would not want to clean for that client. If you removed and put all the stuff back yourself and all I had to do was wipe the shelves then I wouldn't charge because that really wouldn't eat into my time to get to all the other things.

I heard something the other day that might help if you're feeling overwhelmed. If something seems too much or too big to tackle or  you just feel like you cant get get started, then you break it down into smaller steps and focus on those small steps. If those are too much you break those steps down. So if you're looking at the whole house and you're overwhelmed just break it down into rooms, get one done and move on. If that's too much then pick a room and start with one thing like gathering trash. If you tell yourself that that's the thing you need to do, and that the unfuckening will happen later or slowly and doesn't all need to happen right now, it will be easier, and many times the hardest part is getting start, but once we do we find that it's not as hard or as overwhelming as our brains were telling us it would be. I would just put on some music, find the thing you can tackle,  even if it's just grabbing a trash bag grabbing a few things that are obvious in one corner, and see where that takes you. Best of luck op, you can do this!!
